title: Cloudflare connector credentials flow through declared write-only fields
claim: Cloudflare connector credentials are accepted and handed to Host Agent only through schema-declared writeOnly fields. The Kubernetes connector uses put_k8s_secret.data and mounts the Secret as a read-only token file; host managed-file content is writeOnly; container token delivery uses run_instance_command.stdin and writes a mode-0600 token file consumed through --token-file. Host Agent task and capability evidence are projected through declared schemas, and unknown evidence schemas fail closed.
rationale: Credentials placed in generic manifests, shell command arguments, or durable task evidence can outlive the authorized operation and be exposed by logs or process inspection. Typed writeOnly input paths keep credentials out of Opute evidence while allowing the target runtime to store them in its own protected Secret or file.
owner: wunderous/host-agents owns the Cloudflare provider schemas and execution flow, Host Agent writeOnly operation schemas, and evidence projection.

included: Kubernetes namespace, Secret, and Deployment callback sequence
host tunnel runToken and writeOnly managed-file content
container tunnel runToken delivered through run_instance_command.stdin
durable Host Agent task, plan, and capability invocation evidence
excluded: Kubernetes Secret encryption at rest and access control for authorized cluster readers
Cloudflare credential issuance, rotation, and revocation policy
Cloudflared binary provenance beyond the existing caller-provided URI and SHA-256 validation

exception: The credential is intentionally stored in a Kubernetes Secret named <connector-name>-token, a managed host file, or a mode-0600 file at /etc/opute-cloudflare/tunnel-token in a target container so cloudflared can authenticate. Authorized cluster or host principals can read credentials needed by the service; this decision prevents credentials from entering generic Opute task and capability evidence.

required: Typed and compatibility Kubernetes connector schemas declare token writeOnly.

The Kubernetes provider sends token only through put_k8s_secret.data, also writeOnly; generic manifests contain no credential, and the Deployment mounts the Secret as a read-only file without placing the token in environment variables or process arguments.
ensure_host_file.content and run_instance_command.stdin are writeOnly in standalone and Incus schemas.

Container command arguments do not contain the token; stdin writes it under umask 077 to /etc/opute-cloudflare/tunnel-token with mode 0600 and cloudflared reads --token-file using a caller-provided artifact whose version must be 2025.4.0 or newer.
Host Agent task and plan projection redact connector, host-file, and command-stdin secrets using their declared schemas.
Cloudflare operation results declare runToken writeOnly so task-result evidence redacts it.
The plugin manifest, provider handshake version, and reported generation identify version 1.0.1.

revisionBehavior: Any change to a credential-bearing provider schema, nested secret write, host-file/command handoff, or durable projection requires a provider plugin patch version and generation update when the published contract changes, a matching plugin.yaml and runtime report, and focused regression tests. Generic manifests and container argv may never carry connector credentials. Kubernetes connector images and container artifacts must support remotely managed cloudflared --token-file, which requires version 2025.4.0 or newer; the provider verifies caller-provided container artifact SHA-256 but does not infer a version from that digest.
